parole.significato: A hot Piedmontese dip made from salted anchovies, olive oil and garlic.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian bagna càuda (literally “hot bath, hot dip”), from Piedmontese.

parole.significato: A Piedmontese preparation of chocolate containing about 50 percent hazelnut and almond paste.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian gianduia, gianduja, named after Gianduja, a Piedmontese stock character in the commedia dell'arte, in reference to its place of origin. From Piedmontese Giandoja (literally “John-o'-the-jug”).

parole.significato: A narrow breadstick in Italian cuisine.
parole.testo: From Italian grissino, from Piedmontese grissin, ghërsin, diminutive of ghersa (“line, row”).
